title_en: Great Poems and Songs (4/20): Li Qingzhao and the Grief of an Era
note_en: The 把 construction moves the object in front of the verb to show what happens to it: 李清照把……的痛苦都写进了词里 "Li Qingzhao poured all the pain of ... into her ci poems." English keeps the object after the verb, but with 把 the order is subject + 把 + object + verb + result (写进 "write into"). 都 here sums up the object, "all of that pain," even though it comes after it.

sentences.en: When she was young, Li Qingzhao wrote a light, lively poem to the tune "Like a Dream": "I often remember the pavilion by the stream at sunset, so happily drunk I couldn't find the way home. When the fun was over, I rowed back late and strayed deep into the lotus flowers. Paddling hard, paddling hard, I startled a whole shore of gulls and egrets into flight."

sentences.en: Another of her famous poems to the tune "Like a Dream" reads: "Last night the rain was light, the wind was fierce; deep sleep didn't clear away the last of the wine. I ask the maid rolling up the blind, and she says the crabapple blossoms are just as before. Don't you know, don't you know? The green must be lush now, and the red grown thin."
